text: The assembly will hear an address by her
excellency
Taka Ichi Sanai,
Prime Minister of Japan. I request
protocol to escort her excellency and
invite her to address the assembly.
Madame President, excellencies,
the international order is experiencing
a period of great instability. The free
and open international order based on
the rule of law that we have fostered is
facing difficult challenges on multiple
fronts.
Amid a shifting balance of power and
intensifying geopolitical competition,
innocent civilian lives are being lost
around the world every day.
The stable postcold war era is now a
thing of the past. The distribution of
goods is stagnating. People across the
world are suffering from high cost of
living. Progress towards development
goals is not on track and human rights
issues are arising in various places
around the world. Against this backdrop,
has the United Nations now 80 years on
since its foundation been failing to
fulfill its role in promoting peace and
stability around the world? We are even
hearing such concerns today. Madame
President, despite these concerns, the
United Nations has never been more
important than it is today in bringing
about peace and stability to the world
and enabling the international community
to overcome new challenges and prosper.
Japan will continue to fulfill its
significant responsibilities towards the
United Nations and I am here today to
express that resolve.
This year marks the 70th anniversary of
Japan's accession to the United Nations.
In this milestone year, I would first
like to address how Japan has been
tackling the challenges facing the
international community working hand in
hand with the United Nations. Then
together with you all, I would like to
take this opportunity to revisit the
role of the United Nations in the
international community. Madame
President, first let us turn our
attention to escalating international
tensions in the situation in the Middle
East has been growing increasingly tense
and free and safe navigation is
increasingly under challenge in the
straight of Hormuz which is an
international public good. Japan in
cooperation with the international
community has been continuing to engage
in diplomatic efforts with a view to
achieving an early deescalation of the
situation across the Middle East.
Furthermore, supply concerns regarding
fuel, chemical products, and medical
supplies are causing significant impact
on people's lives and business
operations. Due to ris disruptions in
the supply of fertilizers, the risk of
food crisis is mounting with Africa and
Asia being hit particularly hard. For
many years, we have engaged in dynamic
trade in the free and open seas spanning
the Pacific Ocean to the Indian Ocean
and together we have built a strong and
prosperous region. This holds true also
in the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean
Sea. We wish to extend this to Africa as
well to turn it into a main artery for
growth and prosperity. To that end,
exactly 10 years ago, former Prime
Minister Abishzo advocated a free and
open Indo-Pacific FOIP at the Tokyo
International Conference on African
Development TikT held in Kenya. However,
due to the recent intensification of
geopolitical tensions, free trade has
been hampered and stable energy supplies
and supply chains in general have been
disrupted. Amid this situation, in May
this year, I announced the updated free
and open Indo-Pacific FO. There I
appealed that it is essential for
countries to acquire the capabilities to
freely determine their own futures and
resilience across economic,
social and security domains.
Japan places particular emphasis on
following three pillars that embody this
idea.
First, Japan is engaged in strengthening
the resilience of supply chains for
energy and critical minerals.
For global energy security, it is
crucial to ensure free and transparent
energy trade, engage in international
coordination on strengthening oil
stockpiling and enhance collaboration
between producing and consuming
countries. Japan has also launched the
partnership on wide energy resources
resilience Asia power Asia to strengthen
energy and resource supply resilience in
Asia and has been promoting cooperation
in areas such as stockpiling capacity
development and credit provision.
Furthermore, Japan is currently
formulating a comprehensive cooperation
plan aimed at strengthening the economic
and energy resilience of Gulf countries
in the Middle East. Through this
initiative, we will work to further
strengthen the collaboration between the
Asia-Pacific region, including Japan and
the Gulf countries, to ensure a stable
global energy supply. Moreover, concerns
about arbitrary export restrictions are
growing throughout the international
community. Japan is proposing a vision
for strengthening supply chains which
encompasses not only the development of
alternative supply chains supply sources
but also the enhancement of count's
ability to respond to supply disruptions
in particular in the field of critical
minerals. One example is the resilient
and inclusive supply chain enhancement
partnership rise. Under this initiative,
we are cooperating with countries that
produce critical minerals to enable them
to play a greater role in mining,
refining, and processing. In June, we
established Rise Plus. Under the World
Bank Group, AM pledged a contribution of
20 million US to help develop the
infrastructure essential for critical
minerals production. Second, Japan is
devoted to enhancing cooperation towards
peace and stability. Since the end of
the Second World War, Japan has
consistently and seriously pursued
efforts towards nuclear disarmament and
non-prololiferation.
At the very heart of our aspiration for
a world without nuclear weapons lies the
earnest plea of the Hibbakia.
The catastrophic consequences of nuclear
weapons must never be repeated. It is
Japan's mission as the only country to
have ever suffered atomic bombings
during war to lead the efforts of the
international community towards a world
without nuclear weapons. Japan strongly
calls for solidarity within the
international community to maintain and
strengthen the nuclear
non-prololiferation treaty NPT regime to
which both nuclear weapon states and
non-uclear weapon states are parties.
Further, Japan will persistently advance
realistic and practical efforts,
including enhancing the transparency of
nuclear forces and promoting a deeper
understanding of the realities of atomic
bombings. The situations in Ukraine, in
North Korea have reminded the world of
growing risks and threats posed by
nuclear weapons. There are also concerns
regarding the proliferation of nuclear
and missile related technologies through
the strengthening of military
cooperation between Russia and North
Korea. The security of the Indo-Pacific
and Euro Atlantic is inseparable. The
advancement of North Korea's nuclear and
missile programs as well as its use of
malicious cyber activities including
cryptocurrency thefts as source of
funding are clear violations of relevant
security council resolutions and pose a
serious threat to international peace
and security. The full implementation of
Security Council resolutions under the
principle of the complete
denuclearization of North Korea is
essential. Moreover,
the issue of abductions by North Korea
is an ongoing matter with lives at
stake. The abductees are still denying
their freedoms and their families
continue to suffer. This is a matter of
grave concern not only for Japan but for
the international community.
As the abductees and their families are
aging, the abductions issue must be
resolved immediately.
For the sake of the future of both Japan
and North Korea, I am prepared to engage
in dialogue and take concrete action to
establish a mutually fruitful
relationship in accordance with the
Japan DPRK Pyongyang declaration. Third,
Japan will continue to contribute to the
maintenance and development of a free
and open international order based on
the rule of law. Any attempts to
unilaterally change the status quo by
force or coercion are contrary to the
principles enshrined in the charter of
the United Nations and must never be
tolerated anywhere in the world.
Russia's aggression against Ukraine is
the most obvious example. a permanent
member of the security council which is
with a special responsibility for
international peace and security has
initiated an act of aggression against
another country and has vetoed security
council resolutions concerning its own
actions. In this current situation, it
must be said that the security council
is not functioning for international
peace.
Since the end of second world war, Japan
as a peaceloving nation has attached
great importance to the rule of law in
the settlement of any disputes. This is
demonstrated by Japan's consistent
support for and its contrib
contributions of judges to various
international judicial organizations
such as the international court of
justice ICJ, the international criminal
court ICC and the international tribunal
for the law of the sea its we
established a unit for peace mediation
within the government of Japan in March
of this year. Japan will play a more
proactive role in the peaceful
settlement of disputes. Furthermore, the
maritime order based on the rule of law
is currently being greatly shaken in the
straight of Hormuz. Ensuring free and
safe navigation through the state of
Hormuse for all vessels without
additional costs as has been the case is
extremely important not only for the
security of the Middle East but also for
the stability of the global economy as a
whole. Similarly, it is essential to
ensure stability in the Bob el Mandde.
Japan will continue to work closely with
relevant countries and the international
maritime organization IMO towards the
maintenance of the maritime order in the
Middle East.
Madame President, next I would like to
set out Japan's efforts and commitments
towards the United Nations and
multilateralism.
Since becoming a member state of the
United Nations in 1956, Japan has acted
decisively to address global challenges
such as eradication of poverty, economic
and social development, women's
empowerment, climate change, and global
health.
We have done so
through
our official development assistance and
have deepened our solidarity with the
global south. To date, Japan has
provided ODA totaling over 670 billion
US dollars to developing countries and
regions and has dispatched almost 60,000
Japan overseas cooperation volunteers to
99 countries. Additionally, Japan has
been promoting initiatives towards
achieving universal health coverage UHC
across the globe. Since 1993, Japan has
co-organized the TCAT together with
United Nations. TCAT has served as a
platform for reflecting Africa's voice
in the sustainable development goals
SDGs and for Japan to first put forward
the concept of FOYIP. Africa is endowed
with a dynamic young population and
possesses enormous economic potential.
Japan will continue to promote its
diplomacy towards Africa so that Japan
and Africa can become more resilient and
prosperous together. For example, we
will promote industrial development, job
creation, and enhanced connectivity in
Africa. Furthermore, next year I will
host the Pacific Islands leaders meeting
Palm in Yokohama, Japan, which Japan has
convened together with the Pacific
Islands region since 1997.
Japan aims to further deepen our
collaboration with the Pacific Island
count's region and promote the stability
and prosperity of the region, including
addressing common challenges such as
maritime security and climate change.
Several large-scale disasters have
occurred and continuously caused extreme
damage around the world this year,
including in Japan.
Natural disasters are becoming more
severe and frequent. Japan is striving
to become the world's leading nation in
disaster risk reduction. To share
Japan's expertise and technology in
disaster risk reduction and contribute
to global efforts in this field, I
appointed a new minister of state for
international disaster risk reduction
cooperation. In my cabinet reshuffle
last week, I myself in 2015 as minister
for internal affairs and communications
attended the United Nations World
Conference on Disaster Reduction where
the SAI framework for disaster risk
reduction was adopted. Promoting this
framework remains one of our top
priorities to this day. It is in Sai
that Japan will host the Asia-Pacific
Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk
Reduction in October next year. To
protect the lives of present and future
generations, all states must take
serious action to tackle global warming.
I believe that climate action and
economic growth can go hand in hand.
Japan has been advancing green
transformation GS GX efforts with the
goal of achieving
net zero by 2050.
Uh such capabilities include
establishing the basis for the
production and engineering of materials
such as green steel, utilizing the
world's most efficient gas firepower
generation, and popularizing the
adoption of energy efficient data
centers,
harnessing Japan's technological
capabilities. We will enhance these
efforts with a view to strengthening the
resilience of the energy supply demand
structure and vigorously advance the
policy package for wide energy and
resources resilience through green
transformation or power GX. Furthermore,
Japan will contribute to global climate
action including through GX related
efforts such as the Asia zero emission
community
as that simultaneously achieve
decarbonization, energy security and
economic growth. Next year, Japan will
host the World Horicultural Exposition
2027 in Yokohama, which is an industrial
trade fair showcasing green technologies
and approaches to sustainable
development. We sincerely hope that many
of you will come to join this expo.
There are also challenges arising from
technological innovation. Whilst
advances in AI bring tremendous
opportunities for humanity, they also
pose challenges, including those related
no related to national security. We also
urgently need measures to tackle the
spread of information not based on facts
as well as the spread of propaganda.
Japan took the initiative to launch the
Hiroshima AI process, establishing the
world's first internal world's first
international principles and code of
conduct to govern generative AI. In
parallel, Japan has been working with
like-minded partners and global south
partners to co-create a safe, secure,
and trustworthy AI ecosystem and will
enhance cooperation on safety to respond
to the risks of highly capable frontier
AI. To accelerate these efforts, we
intend to host an AI summit in Japan at
the earliest opportunity. Madame
President, since the end of the Second
World War, Japan has built the peace and
prosperity it has today through the
tireless efforts of our predecessors and
the goodwill of a large number of
countries. In the course of these
efforts, Japan itself has consistently
acted in the spirit of multilateralism
towards addressing challenges facing the
international community. However, these
challenges cannot be cannot be solved by
any single country acting alone. Now
more than ever, the flag of the United
Nations must be held high. And under
that banner, member states must mobilize
the collective strength of the
membership to elaborate new rules and
build a framework for cooperation. I am
convinced that the United Nations is the
only organization capable of taking the
helm on a global scale. To this end, as
well, reform of the United Nations is
essential. The United Nations is a
vessel and the responsibility for
determining its contents lies with us,
namely the member states. Rather than
lamenting at the institutional fatigue
of the United Nations, member states
should unite with one heart, vigorously
advance reform of the United Nations and
transform the organization into a more
resilient and effective United Nations.
Let us move forward building on the
achievements of the current Secretary
General Antonio Gutirez. At the same
time, the charter of the United Nations,
which is now 81 years old, should also
be reviewed regarding the so-called
enemy states clauses. A United Nations
General Assembly resolution was adopted
in 2005 to delete references to enemy
states from the charter of the United
Nations expressing the resolve of the
heads of state and government of all
member states. In accordance with this
resolution, these clauses must be
deleted. I would like to strongly
emphasize this position as Japan takes
pride and honor in its significant
contributions to the efforts of the
United Nations for the last 70 years.
Furthermore, as a matter of utmost
importance, reform of the security
council is urgently needed. The current
structure of the security council whose
mandate is to maintain international
peace and security reflects the
international situation as it stood in
We need to transform it without delay
into a structure that truly reflects the
current realities of the international
community. To this end, it is essential
to expand the number of both permanent
and non-permanent members in order to
ensure the legitimacy and
representativeness of the security
council. A majority of member states
support the expansion of both
categories. Japan is determined to
fulfill its solemn responsibility in
these UN reforms.
Madame President, in the 70 years since
we became a UN member state, Japan has
consistently contributed to the peace
and prosperity of the international
community as a peaceloving nation under
its under its exclusively
defenseoriented policy. Furthermore, we
have worked handinhand with United
Nations on the two indispensable tasks
of establishing rules and institutions
and providing support on the ground.
This policy will remain unchanged in the
future. In light of this history, Japan
feels to feels a sense of responsibility
to safeguard the ideals of the United
Nations as our beacon of hope and to
carry that light forward into the
future. To that end, with its renewed
commitment to the United Nations and
multilateralism, Japan will continue to
steadily take actions. Now at a time
when the world is in turmoil, the United
Nations itself must be reborn as a more
resilient and effective United Nations
and regain the trust of the
international community. Together with
this more resilient and effective United
Nations, Japan is determined to create
peace and prosperity by making the
Indoacific and the international
community more resilient and prosperous.
Thank you so very much.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish to
thank the prime minister of Japan.
